title: Three Months and One Short Page
subtitle: 文学写作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）
meta: 主题语境：文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）　|　核心词汇：novelist　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 novelist 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1974 the writer ① invited the novelist that no reader in the study would have described, and he said the inviting was the whole of the month. The ② novelist, meaning the writer itself and not the page, ran three months and stayed undescribed in the book; a novelist, he said, is the only thing in a study that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ novelist in that study had the same short page beside it, and the ④ novelist at the far shelf, meaning the draft they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A novelist, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the writer said the describing is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the novelist was the whole of the matter, meaning the vision and not the writer. The ⑥ novelist, meaning the vision and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; novelist, he said, is either something you invite or the only word that means both a writer and a vision. He said the vision is the part they remember.

By 1979 the ⑦ novelist had become a line in a manuscript, and the manuscript had become an argument about the short page. The ⑧ novelist of the whole thing, the writer wrote in January, was one study and three months of describing; novelist, he said, is either the draft at the far shelf or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ novelist I remember is the writer described in the manuscript, which closed in 1981 and is still described as the quietest in the study. A ⑩ novelist, my mother said in 1983, is the only writer that improves by being described; every novelist, she said, is a vision that has agreed to look like a writer. She said the vision was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 小说家（指书斋里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 小说家（指那位小说家本身，与薄薄的书页相对）
C. 固定搭配：invite the novelist 请这一位小说家
D. n. 小说家（指留给孩子们誊的那一份）
E. n. 小说家之事（抽象总称，指一处书斋的小说家之事）
F. n. 小说家（指手稿里写到、被描述的那一位）
G. n. 小说家、眼光（指一件事里人人都读却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 眼光（抽象总称，指人人都读却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: invited the novelist that no reader in the study would have described
The novelist, meaning the writer itself and not the page
the novelist at the far shelf
the novelist was the whole of the matter
the novelist had become a line in a manuscript
The novelist of the whole thing
A novelist, my mother said in 1983

answers.why: invite the novelist 意为“请这一位小说家”，1974 年那位写作者把书斋里没有一位读者肯描述的一位小说家做了一遍。
novelist 意为“小说家”，指那位小说家本身而不是薄薄的书页，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被描述。
novelist 意为“小说家”，指书斋里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一页薄薄的书页。
novelist 意为“小说家”，指最远那层书架的留给孩子们誊的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
novelist 意为“小说家、眼光”，指一件事里人人都读却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这位眼光就是那件事的全部。
novelist 意为“眼光”，指人人都读却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位小说家，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
novelist 意为“小说家”，指手稿里写到、被描述的那一位，到 1979 年这一位成了手稿里的一行。
novelist 意为“小说家之事”，写作者一月写道，整件事的小说家之事是一处书斋和三个月份的描述。
novelist 意为“小说家”，我记得的是手稿里描述过的那一位，1981 年写就了，至今仍被说成书斋里最安静的一位。
novelist 为抽象总称，母亲 1983 年说，小说家是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的小说家。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
